text:
ConocoPhillips climbed 1.64% today to $132.49, recovering most of the ground lost over the prior four trading days. The bounce reflects broader oil market strength: Brent crude jumped above $90 a barrel following U.S. strikes on Iranian targets, and West Texas Intermediate sits at $83.90—both prices that matter directly to an oil major's earnings. Oil explorers and producers benefit when crude prices rise, since they sell oil at higher prices and their reserves become more valuable.

The past week's volatility and today's recovery also fit into a larger shift in the energy sector's outlook. Major announcements about Venezuela's oil reserves and the White House's focus on boosting U.S. refining capacity suggest renewed political and economic attention on domestic energy supplies, which tends to underpin longer-term confidence in oil companies' prospects.
